articles.title: Solheim Cup golf 2026: Europe take charge against USA after day two foursomes – live
articles.summary: ⛳️ Solheim Cup updates from second day Bernardus Golf ⛳️ Official live scoring | Day one report | And email Matt. Nelly Korda chops an awful tee shot wide right of the par-three 4th green. Team USA’s ball in deep heather.
body: There’s a lovely sense of the Surrey heathland about Bernardus Golf. Nowhere more so than the par-three 11th hole. The trees, the heather, the little ditch, the grass colour. Lottie Woad’s family know it. “It’s like Hankley Common,” they said this morning. But she hasn’t quite clicked on land that ought to make her feel right at home.
On the green, Woad and Charley Hull miss birdie putts. So does Andrea Lee. Can Yealimi Noh convert from seven feet? No, she lips out!
At the par-three 11th Yealimi Noh doesn’t think much of her tee shot - and yet it settles only 8 feet from the flag. She’s not been becalmed for long.

Every match has only one hole in it. The next three hours promise to be dramatic. Europe could build a significant lead. America could pull level. And the visitors could even sneak clear ahead of the singles. It’s game on.

articles.title: Championship roundup: Birmingham sink Derby, West Brom held by QPR
articles.summary: Mepham own goal gave QPR lead in 1-1 draw. Bolton beat Cardiff 1-0 with late Gale header. Callum Styles earned West Brom a point as they came from behind to draw 1-1 against QPR at The Hawthorns.
body: A Chris Mepham own goal put QPR in front in the 38th minute but that lead lasted three minutes as Styles equalised to extend West Brom’s unbeaten home record to 11 games.

The home side had slightly more of the chances but against the run of play Rangers took the lead. Kwame Poku sent Rumarn Burrell racing clear and he turned his man before forcing Max O’Leary into a diving save, only for the rebound to hit Mepham on the head and bounce into the unguarded net.
West Brom levelled when Styles, who was playing in an unfamiliar right-back role, curled home a low shot from just outside the area.

Substitute Thierry Gale headed a 90th-minute winner as Bolton ended a run of four successive Championship defeats with a 1-0 victory over Cardiff. The Barbados international stole in at the far post to convert a left-wing cross from Theo Bair.

articles.summary: Which batter played his most mature innings of the year? Who has given the selectors food for thought? Player ratings from England's win over Pakistan at Edgbaston.
body: England have wrapped up victory over Pakistan in the third Test by eight wickets to seal a 3-0 series win.
Azan Awais - 7 - Still finding his feet at Test level. Made a battling 59 off 84 balls in the second innings, after Pakistan were reduced to 0-2, and looks a player worth persisting with.

Saim Ayub - 1 - Called up for this Test after wholesale changes to the Pakistan side and looked drastically undercooked having not played a first-class fixture since October last year. Almost inevitably he bagged a pair. Scrapes a point for leaving the CPL at the drop of a hat to turn up.
Abdullah Shafique - 1 - Two half-centuries in the series but under leaden skies he was easy meat for Robinson and snared by the Sussex slayer for three and nought.

articles.title: Milwaukee Brewers make MLB history in 20-0 route of Cincinnati Reds
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers went into Friday night as one of the few teams in Major League Baseball without a grand slam this season. Garrett Mitchell gave them their first one of the year, and Milwaukee obliterated the Cincinnati Reds 20-0.
body: Indeed, it was an incredible offensive barrage that led the Brewers to a decisive victory on Friday, combined with Garrett Stallings (who was called up to replace Brandon Sproat ) pitching three scoreless innings of relief for his first career save.

In addition to Mitchell’s grand slam, which was his 10th home run of the year, the Brewers got long balls from William Contreras, Jake Bauers, and Brice Turang. Notably, they no longer rank last in MLB in home runs. Instead of 30th, they rank 29th.
Both Jackson Chourio and Joey Ortiz had four-hit games. Contreras drove in six runs while Turang and Mitchell each drove in four.

Truth be told, the only real disappointing part of the night, if one looks for things to be upset about, was the fact that Christian Yelich was 0-4 after he came in mid-game (after the contest was out of hand). Bo Naylor also got some playing time at first base, but did not record an official at-bat.

articles.title: Guernsey beat Jersey to win historic league meeting
articles.summary: Guernsey beat rivals Jersey 36-19 to win their first league meeting in more than 30 years. The two sides met at St Peter after Jersey were promoted to National Two East in the summer having won the Regional One South Central title win in April.
body: The hosts get off to strong start when Daniel Hawkes went over after four minutes, but Guernsey hit back through a driving maul soon after before Anthony Armstrong scored in the corner to put Guernsey 10-7 up after 24 minutes.

Jersey hit back as George Wilmott got the hosts' second try six minutes before the break with an excellent break from deep but John Dawe scored a third Guernsey try on the stroke of half time as they led 15-14 at the break.
Jersey had Luke Bowles sin-binned early in the second half and Guernsey took full advantage as Matt Creber and Dawe went over to make it 29-14 after 52 minutes.
But Mark Boarer ran in from 55 metres to reduce the gap to 10 points with 25 minutes left.

articles.title: Wolff fumes at 'couch warriors' questioning Mercedes' treatment of Russell
articles.summary: Mercedes chief Toto Wolff has dismissed suggestions from "couch warriors" that the Silver Arrows failed to treat George Russell fairly during the Italian Grand Prix.
body: Russell was narrowly leading the race from his team-mate Kimi Antonelli when Mercedes took a decision to pit the Italian under a virtual safety car.

The call ultimately benefitted Antonelli as he used his fresh tyres to pull off a stunning victory having started from 19th on the grid, which increased Russell's deficit to the Italian at the top of the standings to 66 points.

Speaking to Sky Sports F1 ahead of qualifying at this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix, Wolff reiterated his belief that the fact Antonelli was running on a medium tyre and Russell a hard tyre completely justified the decision.
"It's absolutely the right thing we did," Wolff said. "He (Russell) was on the hard. It was predicted to be a one-stop as the better strategy.

articles.title: MotoGP San Marino GP: Full starting grid
articles.summary: Marco Bezzecchi will start MotoGP's San Marino Grand Prix from pole position after setting a new lap record in Saturday's qualifying session. The factory Aprilia rider smashed the Misano circuit record to clinch his second consecutive pole position, and fourth overall of the season.
body: Reigning world champion Marc Marquez will line up just behind him aboard the factory Ducati, meaning the two title rivals will once again start first and second on the grid.
Completing the front row will be Gresini's Fermin Aldeguer, who made his way from Q1 to grab third place.

The second-row also features several heavy hitters, including VR46's Fabio di Giannantonio and Aprilia's points leader Jorge Martin. Honda rider Luca Marini also impressed in qualifying and will take the start from sixth place.

Alex Marquez appeared set to be in the fight for victory this weekend after practice, but two crashes in qualifying left him ninth, behind KTM's Pedro Acosta and outgoing VR46 rider Franco Morbidelli.

articles.title: Root steers England to series sweep of Pakistan after early scare
articles.summary: England clinched a first home series whitewash of Pakistan despite an early scare by chasing down 130 on day four of the third Test at Edgbaston.
body: The thought of England losing the Test match would have been unthinkable when Ollie Robinson reduced the visitors to 0-2 on the second evening - Pakistan still trailing by 320 at the time - but it looked a genuine possibility when the hosts themselves lost two in their first over to start the fourth morning.
Ben Duckett (0) signed off a miserable series by nicking off first ball to Mohammad Abbas (2-27), who added Emilio Gay (0) lbw to finish a stunning opener.

But any fears of England succumbing to a calamitous defeat were soon dispelled by their skipper as Joe Root (62no) struck a fine fifty, sharing an unbroken 128-run partnership with Jordan Cox (59no), who notched his third half-century late on, to secure victory in 24.2 overs.

Pakistan, meanwhile, will be left wondering would could have been, had Mohammad Ali not overstepped when bowling Root for 23 - dragging onto his stumps off a no-ball - with England just 35-2 at the time.
